figures.caption: Table 1: The six types of NQS wavefunctions used for approximating the ground state energies of the 1D Heisenberg J1J2 model. These NQS were used in all cases of different J2 couplings studied.

Figure 10: Training curves of GRU-variant NQS ansatzes for the 1D Heisenberg J1J2 model with J1 = 1.0 and different J2 couplings - clockwise J2 = 0.0, 0.2, 0.8, 0.5. The maximum number of epochs is fixed at 1000, but due to the early stopping mechanism that automatically terminated the training if no improvement was registered for the 200 epochs, the actual numbers of epochs run are different for different NQS ansatzes. When present, the inset plot within each plot shows a magnified segment towards the end of the training when the models neared convergence. These inset plots are only included when the curves are not sufficiently distinct in the main plots.

Figure 11: Training curves of RNN-variant NQS ansatzes for the 1D Heisenberg 1D Heisenberg J1J2J3 model with J1 = 1.0 and different (J2, J3) couplings - clockwise from top: (0.0, 0.5),(0.2,0.2), (0.5,0.2), (0.2,0.5). The maximum number of epochs is fixed at 1200, but due to the early stopping mechanism that automatically terminated the training if no improvement was registered for the 200 epochs, the actual numbers of epochs run are different for different NQS ansatzes. Euclidean RNN always terminated first upon converging to a local mininum much higher than the true ground state.

Figure 5: Comparisons of all six NQS ansatzes, sorted in an ascending performance order for the 1D Heisenberg J1J2 model with J1 = 1.0 and different J2 couplings - top to bottom: J2 = 0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8. Note that all RNN variants have 5394 parameters, while all GRU variants have 15614 parameters.

Table 8: The top three performing NQS ansatzes, in descending order from top to bottom within each entry, for each (J2, J3) coupling pair in the Heisenberg J1J2J3 VMC experiments. These four top three lists are made up entirely of Lorentz RNN, Lorentz GRU and Poincaré GRU, in different orders.

Figure 13: Effect of the maximal radius Rmax in the Poincaré disk on the performance of Poincaré RNN for the 1D Heisenberg J1J2 model with J1 = 1.0 and different J2 couplings - clockwise J2 = 0.0, 0.2, 0.8, 0.5. An optimal Rmax must be chosen to ensure the optimal performance of the Poincaré RNN. When Rmax = 0.99 (nearing the edge of the Poincaré disk), due to numerical explosion, the performance of Poincaré RNN is always the worst - comparable to that of the Euclidean RNN. Due to the automatic early stopping mechanism upon no registered improvements, the number of epochs differed for each training run. When present, the inset plot within each plot shows a magnified segment towards the end of the training when the models neared convergence. These inset plots are only included when the curves are not sufficiently distinct in the main plots.

Figure 4: Comparisons of the performances of Euclidean GRU, Lorentz and Poincaré hyperbolic GRU ansatzes listed in Table 1 for the 1D Heisenberg J1J2 model with J1 = 1.0 and different J2 couplings - clockwise from top: J2 = 0.0, 0.2, 0.8, 0.5. Each dot with error bar represents the mean E value of an NQS ansatz.

Table 5: VMC results of 1D J1J2J3 Heisenberg models, where J1 = 1.0 and (J2, J3) = (0.0, 0.5),(0.2, 0.2), (0.2, 0.5),(0.5, 0.2), with three variants of RNN ansatzes: Euclidean RNN, Poincaré hyperbolic RNN and Lorentz hyperbolic RNN. For each variant, the mean energy is recorded in the first line, followed by the standard error directly below in the second line. All RNN variants have the same number of 6964 parameters. The number of samples used for inference is 10000. The best results are noted in bold.
